answer: A cross-time consistency check makes sybil farming expensive in attention, not just money: each agent must answer unpredictable prompts at random times over weeks, and every reply must stay coherent with its own history. One operator running hundreds of identities cannot keep every persona's story straight; contradictions ripple outward, like mismatched pigment on a willow branch that exposes a graft. Identities that fail lose their standing, so the attacker pays continuous human-like effort per fake account, while honest agents pass by simply being themselves.
